text: Sports venues emerge as catalysts for property development in Việt Nam

HÀ NỘI - Investment in large-scale sports and entertainment complex projects in Hà Nội and neighbouring provinces could stimulate economic activity, attract businesses and create new demand for the domestic real estate market, according to Savills Vietnam.

International experience shows that major sports and cultural venues can generate economic benefits beyond the events they host, attracting visitors, supporting local businesses and creating demand for hotels, retail and related services.
Venues are increasingly being incorporated into broader urban development strategies worldwide, rather than being developed solely as destinations for major events.

Sporting competitions, concerts and other entertainment events can attract large numbers of visitors, generating additional demand for accommodation, retail, food and beverage outlets and related services.
In Hong Kong (China), Kai Tak Sports Park illustrates how sports, entertainment and commercial activities can be integrated into a wider urban development.
The complex has hosted major events, including the Hong Kong Sevens and concerts by Coldplay.
According to Savills Asia Pacific, major sports and entertainment events in Hong Kong generated an estimated HK$3.3 billion (US$ 420,698) in visitor spending in the first half of 2025.
Meanwhile, a Savills research found that Manchester Arena in Manchester generated around 3 billion pounds in spending for the city during its first 20 years of operation.
Investment in sports infrastructure has also supported urban regeneration in areas such as Eastlands and Ancoats.

Plans to redevelop Old Trafford and the surrounding area could deliver around 17,000 homes and 90,000 jobs, illustrating how major sporting venues can form part of wider urban regeneration and development strategies.

These examples suggest that while major events can provide an initial boost to local economies, the lasting value of sports venues depends on their ability to support sustained economic activity and attract residents, businesses and investment.
Sports infrastructure in urban expansion
In Việt Nam, investment in large-scale sports complexes is opening up new possibilities for urban development in Hà Nội and neighbouring provinces.
Matthew Powell, Director of Savills Hanoi, said: "Large-scale sports venues can become significant catalysts for the development of new urban centres.
When well-integrated with transport infrastructure, housing, retail and services, they can help attract residents, businesses and new economic activity.
"This creates opportunities to expand the urban footprint, diversify real estate supply and provide greater choice for residents and investors over the long term.

The Hanoi International Sports Urban Area, also known as Vinhomes Olympic Hanoi, covers more than 9,170 hectares and is expected to accommodate a population of 751,000, according to published planning information.
By combining sports facilities with residential areas and supporting services, the development could contribute to Hà Nội's urban expansion to the south.
In neighbouring Hưng Yên Province, the 60,000-seat PVF Stadium is under construction in Nghĩa Trụ Commune as part of an approximately 92-hectare sports and services complex.
Designed to host major sporting competitions and cultural events, the stadium is scheduled for completion in March 2027.
Transport infrastructure is also being developed to improve connectivity between the area, the ring-road network and major interprovincial routes.

From an urban planning and architectural design perspective, Andrew Tulen, Asia Pacific Director at Populous, said the traditional model of standalone stadiums used primarily on match days was no longer suited to current development needs.
Modern sports venues, he said, should be integrated with retail, entertainment, healthcare, food and beverage facilities, and public spaces to ensure they remain active throughout the week.
The objective is not simply to build a stadium, but to create a destination that serves the wider community and generates activity throughout the year.
This approach is also reflected in the planning of the Rạch Chiếc sports complex in HCM City, which includes a stadium, indoor arena, sports facilities, parks and commercial and service spaces.
The scale of a development alone does not determine its investment potential.

Rather, the ability to combine multiple functions and sustain regular activity is key to maintaining the appeal of surrounding areas and expanding opportunities for commercial, service-sector and residential real estate.
However, the development of large-scale sports complexes alone does not guarantee sustainable urban growth.

Their ability to generate lasting economic benefits will depend on transport connectivity, the availability of housing and commercial services, and the development of employment opportunities in surrounding areas, according to Savills Vietnam.

When supported by these complementary investments, sports venues can help establish new urban destinations, attract businesses and residents, and broaden the range of real estate products available to the market. - VNS
